Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Repair or replace damaged wooden structures or components
Situation2: A house has structural wood damage from termites, and the carpenter needs to provide an urgent repair plan
Story:
My phone buzzed just as I was packing up my tools after a long day. It was Mark, my oldest friend, his voice shaky. “My car broke down on the highway. I’m scared, can you come get me? Please.” I glanced at the clock—almost midnight. I promised I’d be there, but as I hung up, my other phone rang. It was Mrs. Patel, her voice trembling. “The termites have eaten through the main beam. The inspector says the house isn’t safe. Can you come tonight? I don’t know where else to turn.” 

I felt my chest tighten. Mark was counting on me, stranded and scared. But Mrs. Patel’s house could collapse if I didn’t act fast. Both needed me, right now, for completely different reasons. I could hear the desperation in both their voices, and I felt torn in two. My hands shook as I stared at my keys, the weight of both expectations pressing down on me, unsure which way to turn.
